name: Sentry (Functional Software, Inc.)
origin_detail: David Cramer started Sentry around 2008 as an open-source Django error-logging project; he and Chris Jennings founded Functional Software, Inc. in San Francisco around 2012 to sell hosted Sentry.
openness_notes: Sentry was BSD-3-Clause, with revenue mainly from its hosted SaaS. In 2019 it moved to BSL 1.1 (converting to Apache-2.0 after three years). In 2023 it wrote the Functional Source License (FSL), which converts to Apache-2.0 or MIT after two years. It now promotes 'Fair Source' and funds maintainers through the Open Source Pledge. Source-available and non-OSI today: level 1.

license_history.license: Functional Source License (2-year change date to Apache-2.0/MIT)

relicensing_events.outcome_note: No significant fork known; the product is mostly consumed as SaaS (unverified)
Shorter delay before code becomes open source; still non-OSI (unverified)

robustness: Single-vendor. Delayed-open licences guarantee that code older than two years becomes Apache/MIT, so an eventual open fork path exists by design.
openness_effect_assessment: Not assessed: no sourced research was possible in this session.
key_takeaway: Draft only. Sentry authored the 'fair source' model: source-available now, open source after a delay. It suggests a SaaS-first company can close its licence with little community fracture when most users consume the hosted service.
